Why I keep a paper notebook next to my keyboard

Essay · 7 min read · Written by a person, on a Sunday

Every tab I open is a small promise to come back. Most of those promises are broken by lunch. The notebook is where I write the one thing I actually came to do, before the browser has a chance to suggest twelve others.

It started as an experiment: one week, one page a day, nothing digital allowed on it. By Wednesday I noticed that the list on paper was shorter than the list in my head, and that I finished it.

Paper is slow on purpose. You cannot paste into it, it has no feed, and it never asks whether you are sure you want to leave. That friction is the whole point.
